import test from 'node:test';

describe('suite', () => {
  // assert pos has a run of six: expect, await expect, assert.equal, assert(),
  // an expect chain with not, assert.strictEqual. console.log ends the run.
  it('assert pos', async () => {
    expect(1).toBe(1);
    await expect(p).resolves.toBe(1);
    assert.equal(a, b);
    assert(ok);
    expect(a).not.toBe(2);
    assert.strictEqual(a, 1);
    console.log('not an assertion');
  });

  // assert neg has two runs of five: the longest is 5.
  it('assert neg', () => {
    expect(1).toBe(1);
    expect(2).toBe(2);
    expect(3).toBe(3);
    expect(4).toBe(4);
    expect(5).toBe(5);
    console.log('break');
    expect(1).toBe(1);
    expect(2).toBe(2);
    expect(3).toBe(3);
    expect(4).toBe(4);
    expect(5).toBe(5);
  });

  describe('nested', () => {
    // dup a and dup b share four identical assertions.
    it.only('dup a', () => {
      expect(got.a).toBe(1);
      expect(got.b).toBe(2);
      expect(got.c).toBe(3);
      expect(got.d).toBe(4);
    });

    test('dup b', () => {
      expect(got.a).toBe(1);
      expect(got.b).toBe(2);
      expect(got.c).toBe(3);
      expect(got.d).toBe(4);
      check();
    });
  });

  // near a and near b share only three identical assertions.
  it('near a', () => {
    expect(want.a).toBe(1);
    expect(want.b).toBe(2);
    expect(want.c).toBe(3);
    expect(want.d).toBe(4);
  });

  it('near b', () => {
    expect(want.a).toBe(1);
    expect(want.b).toBe(2);
    expect(want.c).toBe(3);
    expect(want.e).toBe(5);
  });

  it.each([[1], [2]])('each %i', (n: number) => {
    expect(n).toBe(n);
  });
});

// node:test style: t.* calls are assertions, t.diagnostic is not.
test('node style', async (t) => {
  t.assert.equal(1, 1);
  t.assert.ok(true);
  t.diagnostic('x');
  t.assert.equal(2, 2);
});

// helper is not a test callback: its assertions are not measured.
function helper() {
  expect(1).toBe(1);
}
